result.stdout:
Lint SQL files for Aurora DSQL compatibility

Usage: dsql-lint [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...  SQL files to lint (use '-' to read from stdin)

Options:
      --fix                Fix mode: output DSQL-compatible SQL to a new file. Note: SQL comments in modified statements will not be preserved
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>    Output file path (only with --fix and a single input file)
      --format <FORMAT>    Output format [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
      --dialect <DIALECT>  Source SQL dialect. `postgres` (default) lints/fixes PostgreSQL or pg_dump DDL. `mysql` first translates mysqldump-shaped MySQL DDL to DSQL-compatible SQL (requires --fix); MySQL is a fix-only dialect [default: postgres] [possible values: postgres, mysql]
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version

EXIT CODES:
  0  Clean (no issues) or all issues fixed without warnings
  1  Errors found (lint mode) or unfixable errors remain (fix mode)
  2  Usage error (invalid arguments)
  3  Fix mode only: all issues fixed, but some produced warnings

CI USAGE:
  Exit code 3 means the fix succeeded but produced warnings (e.g., removed
  foreign keys). In shell scripts with set -e or CI pipelines, handle it:

    dsql-lint --fix input.sql; rc=$?
    if [ $rc -eq 1 ]; then echo 'unfixable errors'; exit 1; fi
    # rc 0 or 3: fix succeeded (3 = review warnings)
